About This Job
About us: The Endpoint Infrastructure team play a pivotal role in ensuring Students have access to the applications and end-user services they need to support their learning. They package, deploy, upgrade and repair applications that are specified by course leaders and faculties. The University has recently supplemented its SCCM and Jamf Pro environment with AppsAnywhere, a virtual application solution to help manage the larger end-user device base following the move to more remote learning.
About the role: The Endpoint Infrastructure Engineer’s role is to provide best practice technical expertise in the operation and improvement of the University’s end-user computing environment and services. This role will also assist in the design, implementation and maintenance of enterprise quality end-user systems and services to meet the needs of the University in the present and future. For a full list of requirements please see the attached job description.
The successful candidate will have experience of an enterprise scale IT Endpoint infrastructure and will be used to evaluating and delivering solutions and proposing enhancements in order to provide the best possible endpoint management at UWE.
About UWE: We are a well-established university, with over 30,000 students, 250,000 alumni and 3,600 staff. UWE Bristol is one of the largest providers of Higher Education in the South West. We are globally connected and regionally embedded, with strong employer and partner connections. Students come to study with us from all over the UK, as well as from 140 different countries, making this a diverse and interesting place to study. We achieved 89% overall student satisfaction in the National Student Satisfaction survey in 2018, this excellent result puts us as the top university in the South West and in 7th place nationally. In 2019 we were placed in the Guardian’s Top 30 Universities in the UK and we achieved TEF Gold status.
Bristol itself is a hub of social and cultural activity and is a big pull for students and employers alike. A place with a strong, creative and fiercely independent mindset. A city with a buzzing music scene, great restaurants and interesting business ventures. It’s not surprising Bristol is consistently named as one of the best places to live and work in the UK.
This post is based at our lively Frenchay campus where we have invested in the latest facilities and resources to give our students access to everything they need to succeed – with £300m having been spent recently on new state-of-the-art learning spaces and accommodation to enhance our offer even further. Frenchay campus is within close proximity to excellent motorway links and within walking distance of two train stations, making UWE Frenchay Campus the ideal place to work for those wishing to commute to Bristol.
Further information
This is a permanent post and is full-time working 37 hours per week.
This post is available on a job share basis for applicants wishing to work part time.
The University’s normal practice is that new appointments will be made at the starting point of the grade.
In addition to progressive pay rates, UWE Bristol offers a wide range of employee benefits including:
·A generous holiday allowance of 27 days pro rata, increasing to 30 days after 5 years’ continuous service.
·Up to 12.5 bank holiday/closure days per year
·Flexible working (normal office hours 8.30 – 17.00)
·Excellent defined benefit pension schemes
·Access to employee assistance programme
·Ongoing learning and development opportunities
·Family friendly policies and wellbeing initiatives
·Onsite nursery at our Frenchay Campus.
·Savings on purchases via Wider Wallet scheme
·Option to participate in the cycle to work scheme
UWE is committed to supporting and promoting equality and diversity to create an inclusive working environment. We believe this can be achieved through attracting, developing, and retaining a diverse range of staff from many different backgrounds who share our ambition to be a university recognised for the success and impact of our practice-oriented programmes; our strong industry networks and our inclusive global outlook.
We are able to sponsor qualifying candidates for this role under the Home Office Skilled Worker visa route. Please read our Skilled Worker Guidance to assess if you will be eligible to be sponsored under the criteria.
Please also refer to the Home Office Right to Work Checklist which provides details of which documents are acceptable to prove your right to work in the UK. Should you be shortlisted you will be asked to produce your right to work documents at your interview.

About This Job
We are looking for an experienced Senior Land Surveyor to help establish and develop our land surveying capability in Ireland.
This is a senior, hands-on position with responsibility for delivering survey projects from initial enquiry and scope review through to fieldwork, processing, quality assurance and final client deliverables. The successful candidate will be capable of working independently, making sound technical decisions and engaging directly with clients, while having access to the wider SOCOTEC UK & Ireland surveying team for specialist support and additional resources when required.
Projects will span infrastructure, construction, development and the built environment across Ireland, using modern geomatics technologies including robotic total stations, GNSS, digital levels and laser scanning systems.
Key responsibilities include:
• Plan, manage and deliver topographical, land, engineering and construction surveys
• Review tender documentation, technical specifications and client scopes to establish survey requirements and appropriate methodologies
• Undertake detailed topographical surveys across buildings, structures, roads, rail, earthworks, utilities and other site features
• Establish and verify survey control networks
• Undertake construction setting-out, as-built and verification surveys where required
• Process, check and validate survey data prior to issue
• Produce survey drawings, digital terrain models, point clouds, reports and other project deliverables
• Maintain appropriate survey quality assurance, checking and data-management procedures
• Prepare or contribute to survey methodologies, programmes and technical tender submissions
• Liaise directly with clients, consultants, contractors and project teams
• Identify opportunities for additional surveying services and support the growth of the Ireland surveying capability
• Provide technical guidance and mentoring to junior survey staff as the team develops
• Collaborate with SOCOTEC surveying, monitoring, engineering and specialist teams on multidisciplinary projects
• Ensure work is delivered safely, efficiently and in accordance with client requirements and company procedures

Qualifications
We are looking for someone with:
• Significant practical experience in land, topographical, engineering or geomatics surveying
• The ability to independently plan, undertake, process and deliver survey projects
• Strong knowledge of survey control, coordinate systems, GNSS, robotic total stations and levelling techniques
• Experience producing and checking professional topographical and engineering survey deliverables
• Experience reviewing technical specifications, tender documentation and scopes of work
• Competence with industry-standard survey processing and CAD software
• Strong understanding of survey accuracy, verification and quality control
• Confidence dealing directly with clients and providing technical advice
• Good organisational and project-management skills
• Commercial awareness and an interest in helping develop a growing service
• A full driving licence and willingness to travel throughout Ireland and the UK when required
Experience in laser scanning, point-cloud processing, UAV surveying, precise levelling, monitoring, BIM or other specialist geomatics techniques would be advantageous.

Additional Information
What's in it for you?
Your expertise deserves recognition. Alongside a competitive salary, we offer a comprehensive benefits package including:
• Company pension
• Electric car scheme, where applicable
• Employee recognition programmes
• Family-friendly support
• Exclusive employee retail discounts
• Employee Assistance Programme
• Access to professional training, qualifications and career development
This role gives you the chance to play a key part in developing SOCOTEC’s surveying service in Ireland, with the autonomy to take ownership of projects and direct access to the technical expertise and resources of the wider SOCOTEC UK & Ireland surveying team.
SOCOTEC UK & Ireland is committed to creating an inclusive working environment and is proud to be a Disability Confident employer.

About This Job
AFRY offers a challenging career path in one of the world’s leading energy industry consultants.
Due to the growth of our business we have a new opportunity for an Experienced Scientist, Engineer or Mathematician to join an expanding team of Safety and Reliability specialists in AFRY’s Nuclear Business Unit. The successful candidate will assist with the development and implementation of a variety of projects in nuclear safety and reliability services for a wide range of domestic and international clients.
You will contribute to projects in the following areas: Hazard Identification techniques, Safety and Hazard Analysis, Quantified Risk Assessment, Engineering design substantiation, Option studies, Plant and Site licensing, Safety case documentation production, review and update, Management and development of new and existing client relationships, Management of small and larger scale projects, Mentoring emerging talent.

Qualifications
It would be great if you had some of the following skills, but don’t worry if you don’t tick every box, we’ll help you develop along the way.
• Science or Engineering degree in a relevant STEM subject;
• Experience in the nuclear sector;
• An aptitude for quantitative and qualitative analysis, including statistics;
• The ability to explain complex information in a clear and logical way;
• Due to the sensitive classification of the work this position is only available to British nationals who have the ability to hold appropriate level of UK security clearance for projects;
• You will be working in a commercial environment against budgets and deadlines so you will need to be able to think for yourself, be pro-active and have a business-oriented mindset;
• We work with clients across the UK so a willingness to work away from your home office on UK projects for extended periods of time or abroad.
One or more of the following would be an advantage but is not essential:
• Experience in system safety analysis, including fault tree analysis and event tree analysis.
• Track record of delivering technically challenging projects.
• Experience working on projects in the nuclear industry.
• Professional recognition with an appropriate body is an advantage but not essential, if you are currently working towards professional recognition assistance will be provided.

Additional Information
At AFRY, we believe in the importance of inclusion and so we welcome and cherish diverse experiences, perspectives, and backgrounds. We are actively looking for qualified candidates irrespective of gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religion, disability, age, or periods of unemployment. We recognise that there are many reasons for taking time between jobs, from caregiving responsibilities to continuing education and we view these as positive aspects of your CV.
You will be part of a global company where our diversity is our strength.
We value a healthy work-life balance and are committed to your wellbeing. We are open to flexible working arrangements, including part-time, flexible working patterns and we operate a hybrid working environment.
We offer a competitive salary and an excellent range of benefits, including 25 days holiday each year, private medical insurance, life assurance and a pension scheme.
As part of your application process, please provide a CV and covering letter stating why you want to work for AFRY, what you can offer through the role and your salary expectations. We only accept online applications.
You must have the right to live and work in the UK.  A full driving licence valid in the UK is required.
No Recruitment Agency applications please.
At AFRY, we engineer change in everything we do. Change happens when brave ideas come together. When we collaborate, innovate technology, and embrace challenging points of view. That’s how we're making future. We are actively looking for qualified candidates to join our inclusive and diverse teams across the globe. Join us in accelerating the transition towards a sustainable future.

About This Job
Start here. Grow here.
With unprecedented opportunity across the UK and Ireland Water industry, AECOM’s Water business is seeking a Capture Management Lead to join the Water Strategy & Growth team.
In this pivotal leadership role, you will be responsible for driving strategic growth and securing major enterprise-level critical pursuits (typically £25m + revenue) in the Water sector. This position requires visionary leadership, strategic thinking, and the ability to lead and take full ownership of capture & positioning strategies. Reporting to the Strategy & Growth Director for Water, the role will require developing and implementing winning capture and client positioning strategies, fostering collaboration across global and regional business lines, and ensuring operational excellence throughout the pursuit lifecycle. The role offers flexibility, with remote/virtual work options and travel as required.
Key Responsibilities:
Strategic Leadership & Business Development
• Lead and win enterprise critical pursuits (ECP / Tier 2) as the Capture Lead, owning the pursuit strategy from identification through to submission.
• Direct discovery, pre-positioning, differentiation, and delivery strategies for major transformative programmes including both new business opportunities and the renewal / extension of existing strategic opportunities within key accounts.
• Own pursuit governance, bid budgets, winning pursuit team composition and partnering / supply chain selection.
• Lead a holistic approach to capture strategy development, including client listening, win strategy, solution development, marcomms planning, bid planning & review through to debrief & lessons learnt.
• Establish and nurture client relationships to identifying bespoke needs, leveraging proactive engagement to inform and validate solutions.
• Analyse competitive landscapes, leveraging insights from recent wins and losses to refine strategies.
• Help to build and maintain a diversified pipeline of qualified opportunities, ensuring alignment with business strategy and goals.
• Collaborate with global and regional leaders to develop and execute growth plans aligned with AECOM’s strategic priorities.
• Partner with Client Account Managers, Market Sector Leaders, and other business line representatives to leverage Our Client Promise in delivering capture outcomes that align with client expectations.
Team Collaboration & Mentorship
• Partner with bid, marketing, technical, operations and commercial teams to prepare Capture Plans for complex proposals.
• Drive cultural change in approach to capture, facilitating the adoption of AECOM’s positioning and pursuit playbooks and roll out of supportive training across Water.
• Facilitate pursuit strategy meetings and provide guidance and coaching for client engagement/positioning, presentation and interview teams.
• Promote a collaborative approach, leveraging multidisciplinary teams from across the region and globe to achieve success.
• Guide technical writers to develop dynamic and compelling content (all channels not just RFP), that is both compliant and compelling / persuasive.
• Ensure partnership between technical, marketing and bidding staff for proposal best practices.
Operational Excellence
• Drive integrated strategies to improve capture and win rates and secure transformative programs.
• Champion the complete sales lifecycle aligned to best practice, including ensuring quality assurance and adherence to Green Light Analysis and Go/No-Go rigor.
• Coordinate with strategic marketing to plan and execute effective pursuit-based positioning campaigns that supports client positioning/engagement and elevated brand awareness.
• Ensure compliance with commercial, financial, legal, and governance elements of opportunities and contracts.
• Drive accountability for delivering sales metrics and achieving high capture/win rates.
Innovation & Impact
• Position AECOM’s innovative solutions, including sustainability & ESG, digitalisation, and equity-focused initiatives, to meet client transformation agendas.
• Leverage AECOM’s ‘Think & Act Global’ expertise and enterprise capabilities to deliver value-driven, client-focused outcomes.
• Harness potential of key growth enablers such as digital and technological innovations, including AI and autonomy, to provide competitive advantage in a rapidly changing world.
Influence & Relationship Management
• Build trust with client decision-makers, delivery partners and internal stakeholders, including Client Account Managers, Market Sector Leaders, Regional Business Line Leaders, and Executive Boards.
• Innovative thinker, problem solver and willing to challenge teams to stretch beyond the norm.
• Demonstrate resilience and adaptability, ensuring focus remains on those opportunities which will deliver growth ambitions and provide greater value to our clients.
Enjoy the Perks.
At AECOM, you'll enjoy a range of core and personalised benefits designed to support your future and well-being, customised to fit your lifestyle. Take advantage of career development opportunities, our flexible hybrid working model to ensure a work-life balance that suits your lifestyle, technical practice networks, AECOM University, and volunteering days. We recognise that everyone’s circumstances are different, so we’re more than happy to discuss part-time or flexible working arrangements.

Qualifications
Ready to push the limits of what’s possible?
Here’s what we’re looking for:
• Degree level relevant qualification (preferable)
• Demonstrated leadership experience of critical pursuit capture strategy development and alignment with business targets and growth strategy within a consultancy environment.
• Proven track record of successfully leading strategic and complex pursuit strategies (Net Service Revenue above £25m) across multi-disciplinary and multi-locational teams, including working alongside clients, delivery partners and supply chain.
• Proven ability to deliver sales metrics and develop compelling client-centric value proposition.
• Demonstrated ability to collaborate at all organisational levels – strong leadership skills with experience of building and managing large and diverse pursuit/capture teams.
• Relevant Water Industry experience together with working in a global matrix organisation (preferable).

Additional Information
We celebrate diversity, including neurodiversity, and believe it enriches our team. We welcome applications from all backgrounds and abilities. If you are an applicant with a disability that requires reasonable accommodation to complete the application process, please contact us at ReasonableAccomodations@aecom.com.
At AECOM, we value everyone's unique contributions and perspectives. If you meet some of the requirements above or have transferable skills you believe would benefit us, we would be delighted to hear from you!
Interested in the role or curious about life at AECOM? Follow us on LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagr

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/genomicsengland.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Network Architect
We’re looking for an accomplished Network Architect to join our Scalable Tech Team at Genomics England and provide technical leadership for the secure, resilient connectivity that underpins our technology platform, healthcare, research and corporate services.
Our network services connect cloud platforms (primarily AWS) and on-premise infrastructure, enabling clinicians, researchers and colleagues to access sensitive genomic and associated health data securely and reliably.
Working within the Technology and Product Directorate, you’ll shape and deliver Genomics England’s network architecture across AWS, hybrid connectivity, corporate locations and partner integrations. You’ll collaborate with infrastructure, cloud platform, security, engineering, procurement, commercial, service management and delivery colleagues to turn complex operational and user needs into coherent, cost-effective, scalable and secure network solutions.
This is an architecture role where you’ll balance longer-term network strategy with practical delivery. Drawing on your proven experience as an Architect, you will guide teams through network architecture decisions, develop reusable standards and patterns, and ensure solutions align with Genomics England’s wider technology strategy, architecture standards, security requirements and service expectations.
The scale and sensitivity of genomics require high-performing, highly available networks. AWS is at the heart of our environment, alongside hybrid and third-party connectivity, supporting secure data transfer, high-performance compute, large-scale storage, research workflows, operational services and controlled access to sensitive data.
Key Responsibilities
•
Lead the architecture and design of network solutions across Genomics England, ensuring they are secure, scalable, cost-effective, resilient, supportable and aligned with organisational needs. Define target architectures, standards and reusable patterns for cloud, hybrid, remote-access and partner connectivity.
•
Design and govern AWS networking, including multi-account connectivity, VPC design, routing, segmentation, private connectivity, DNS, load balancing and network security controls. Architect resilient connectivity between AWS, Genomics England locations, NHS and government partners, research organisations, suppliers and other trusted environments.
•
Work with security colleagues to embed zero-trust principles, least privilege, network segmentation, secure remote access, encryption in transit and effective boundary protection. Ensure network designs support the secure movement and processing of large-scale genomic and associated health data, including high-throughput and latency-sensitive workloads.
•
Develop network roadmaps and transition architectures that balance strategic direction, technical debt, service continuity and delivery priorities. Provide architectural oversight from discovery and options analysis through implementation, migration and live service.
•
Document network architectures, traffic flows, trust boundaries, technical options, decisions, dependencies and transition states clearly for technical and non-technical audiences. Define requirements for network observability, performance monitoring, capacity management, configuration control, resilience testing and incident response.
•
Collaborate with cloud platform, infrastructure, engineering, security, service management and delivery teams to ensure designs can be implemented and operated effectively. Contribute to architecture governance and assurance, presenting network designs and recommendations through appropriate technical forums.
•
Identify network risks, constraints, dependencies and single points of failure early, working with teams to address them. Evaluate emerging networking technologies and managed services where they could improve security, performance, resilience, operability or cost-effectiveness.
•
Work with architects across Genomics England to create coherent end-to-end solutions and encourage appropriate reuse across services. Contribute to architecture best practice and improving the quality of architecture across Genomics England.
Skills and Experience for Success
•
Substantial experience designing and delivering enterprise network architectures in complex, security-conscious environments, with strong knowledge of AWS networking services and patterns, including VPCs, Transit Gateway, Direct Connect, VPN, Route 53, load balancing, private endpoints and network security controls.
•
Experience designing hybrid and multi-site connectivity, routing, switching, segmentation, firewalls, DNS, IP address management, load balancing and secure remote access. Detailed knowledge of physical network technology, ideally Cisco, NVIDIA and Mellanox, and in-depth understanding of Cisco Nexus Dashboard, data centre fabrics, Aruba networking infrastructure, BGP, OSPF, RoCE v2, performance optimisation and lifecycle management.
•
Experience architecting highly available and resilient networks with clear recovery objectives, diverse connectivity and tested failover arrangements. Strong understanding of network security architecture, zero-trust principles, defence in depth, trust boundaries and secure connectivity to third parties.
•
Experience designing networks for high-throughput, data-intensive or latency-sensitive workloads and diagnosing performance or capacity constraints. Good understanding of automation, infrastructure as code, configuration management, observability and operational support for modern networks.
•
Ability to translate business, security, operational and user needs into practical network designs, standards and delivery roadmaps, balancing strategic architectural direction with immediate delivery needs, legacy constraints and service continuity.
•
Experience working with multidisciplinary teams and building alignment across architecture, infrastructure, cloud, engineering, security, procurement, commercial, service management and delivery stakeholders. You are the bridge between a product team's business flow and a working AI capability: you know the AI service catalogue well enough to match the right service to the problem, you help teams build AI-first applications on top of it, and when a gap exists, you make sure the right thing gets built to close it.

MUFG Investor Services are seeking an experienced senior lawyer (12 months FTC) to add to a small but global legal team working in the London office. The successful candidate will have a broad experience of commercial law and be expected to advise the business on legal matters, risk management and maintain commercial strategies.
Scope of work
•
Global Contract Drafting & Negotiation
Review, draft, negotiate, and advise on a wide range of vendor agreements across global jurisdictions. This includes identifying, assessing, and escalating contractual risks in collaboration with Vendor Management, Outsourcing, Data Protection, Legal, Information Security, and business stakeholders. Agreements may include Master Services Agreements (MSAs), Statements of Work (SOWs), Software Licence Agreements, SaaS Agreements, Engagement Letters, and Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs).
•
Regulatory Advisory & Contract Compliance
Provide legal and regulatory guidance on commercial contracts across key MUFG jurisdictions. Advise on regulatory frameworks impacting third-party vendor arrangements, including outsourcing and operational resilience requirements. Support contract remediation, implementation, and ongoing monitoring of regulatory developments to ensure contractual compliance and risk mitigation.

End-to-End Contract Management
Manage vendor contracting matters throughout the full contract lifecycle, from initial instruction through to execution. Responsibilities include gathering and assessing information, advising on appropriate legal approaches, managing timelines and stakeholder expectations, drafting and reviewing documentation, and coordinating input from business teams and external counsel where required.

Vendor Management Partnership
Work closely with Vendor Management, Procurement, and Legal teams to enhance contracting processes, governance frameworks, and review procedures. Facilitate approvals, secure stakeholder sign-off, and provide final legal review and guidance as appropriate.

Stakeholder Advisory
Serve as a trusted legal advisor to operational teams, control and support functions, client-facing teams, senior management, and governance committees. Provide pragmatic advice on legal, regulatory, and contractual matters impacting vendor relationships and business operations.
•
Financial Services Expertise
Leverage a strong understanding of the financial services environment to assess legal and regulatory risks, support business initiatives, and provide commercially sound legal advice aligned with industry requirements.
•
Project Support & Change Initiatives
Support strategic and regulatory projects that impact vendor relationships, third-party risk management, and contractual frameworks. Contribute legal expertise to business transformation, remediation, and governance initiatives.
•
Additional Responsibilities
Undertake other ad hoc legal matters, projects, and responsibilities as required to support the wider Legal and business functions.

Qualifications
Qualified English solicitor with at least 5-10 years PQE (must be admitted to the Law Society of England and Wales and be in good standing)

Job Description
We're looking for an experienced Senior Product Engineer to join the Risk & Control Governance team / Risk Assessment Group. You'll be instrumental in building the governance, assurance, and data foundations that ensure every risk decision at Wise is consistent, explainable, auditable, and continuously monitored.
This role works at the intersection of the Risk API platform, Product, and Financial Crime (FinCrime) teams — offering a unique opportunity to build the systems that give Wise confidence in every risk assessment it operates at scale.
You will be the driving force behind the platform's trustworthiness and integrity, focusing on:
•
Data Governance: Building and maintaining data ownership, lineage, and quality monitoring systems that ensure every risk decision is powered by trusted data.
•
Control Assurance: Designing continuous monitoring and validation systems that verify controls perform as intended — including trigger validation, drift detection, coverage analysis, and control health scoring.
•
Auditability & Explainability: Implementing end-to-end audit trails, change history tracking, and explainability tooling that enables one-click regulatory evidence generation.
•
Scalable Solutions: Designing robust, high-throughput solutions that handle large volumes of data and can be quickly understood and scaled across multiple distinct risk domains.
What will you be working on?
You will join the team at a pivotal moment, with your contributions being immediately visible and critical to the success of the entire Risk Assessment platform's governance layer.
The core challenge for the team — and your immediate focus — is to build the assurance and governance foundations that the platform currently lacks, ensuring every control can answer: Was the right trigger used? Was the right data available? Was the right decision made? Is the control still effective?
Your immediate impact will be to:
•
Build Data Trust: Implement data quality monitoring, data contracts, and lineage tracking that give the organisation full traceability from risk decisions back to source data.
•
Deliver Continuous Assurance: Design and build automated monitoring systems that continuously validate control effectiveness — detecting drift, false positives/negatives, and coverage gaps before they become incidents.
•
Enable Auditability: Create audit trail infrastructure and explainability tooling that dramatically reduces the effort required for regulatory reporting and compliance evidence generation.
•
Integrate with Risk API: Work closely with the Risk API team to embed governance and assurance capabilities into the core platform, ensuring clean integration points and shared data contracts.
Qualifications
What do you need?
•
Strong Backend Engineering: Proven experience building high-throughput, data-intensive systems in any language. Hands-on expertise with Kafka, SQL and NoSQL databases, and designing for scale and reliability.

Data Engineering Aptitude: Experience with data quality frameworks, pipeline orchestration, or lineage tracking. You understand what it takes to make data trustworthy at scale.

Systems Thinking: Ability to reason about complex distributed systems, identify failure modes, and design solutions that are both robust and operationally simple.
•
Ownership & Autonomy: Comfortable operating with ambiguity, defining your own work from high-level objectives, and driving delivery end-to-end without close direction.
•
Collaborative Mindset: Ability to work effectively across team boundaries — particularly with the Risk API team, Product, and FinCrime stakeholders — to align on contracts, data models, and integration patterns.

About This Job
Self-employed / No-contract / Temporary / Part-time / Shift-work
https://flex.amazon.co.uk/recruiting-cities/london per hour* based on delivering a number of parcels across an estimated length of time (referred to as a block).
Deliveries will be collected from the depot in Croydon and will be made to the surrounding areas.
Deliver packages locally and get paid weekly. Flexible hours. Be your own boss.
What is Amazon Flex?
It's simple! You use your own vehicle and your smartphone to deliver packages locally for Amazon as a way of earning extra money weekly to move you closer to your goals. Schedule a delivery block and start delivering parcels as little or as often as you like.
Who can deliver for Amazon Flex?
To become a Delivery Driver you need a valid UK driving licence and a vehicle. Currently the only available delivery options are for owners of a 4-door car or van.You will need to be entitled to work in the UK and pass a background and criminal record check which includes, but is not limited to, a review of driving licence records. Current Amazon employees are not eligible to be Delivery Partners.
How do I sign up?
Grab your mobile and visit the Amazon Flex website to download the app for iPhone or Android. After the download, the app guides you step-by-step through the onboarding process. Once you have passed your background and criminal record check, you will be able to schedule a block and start delivering smiles!
How long are the blocks?
Blocks vary in length, from 1 to 5 hours, depending on the delivery service you support. For example, 1-hour and 2-hour blocks are available for Prime Now deliveries, where customers receive their deliveries within a few hours of making their order. However, for https://www.amazon.co.uk/ deliveries, the area served is larger. In those cases, it's not feasible to have 1-hour or 2-hour blocks and the available blocks are 4-hour and 5-hour.
Money Matters. Know your earnings.
When you schedule a delivery block, you'll know estimated duration and your total payments all before your delivery block begins. You can build your own schedule, there are delivery blocks available seven days a week. However, the available delivery blocks may fluctuate week-to-week and are not guaranteed.
Adjust your work not your life.
Perhaps you have a job but want to supplement your income. Or maybe you are already a delivery driver and want something to keep you busy on the quieter days. Whatever your situation Amazon Flex can offer you the freedom and flexibility to be your own boss and earn extra cash on your own schedule.
No matter what drives you, Amazon Flex helps you get there. Sign-up today.
* Earnings estimates are based on delivering a number of packages across an estimated length of time (referred to as a block), completed while driving a standard motorised vehicle. Should Amazon Flex introduce blocks eligible to be delivered using scooters or other alternative modes of transportation, different rates may apply. We aim to ensure that the number of packages you are assigned to deliver within your block is realistic, taking into account congestion and the primary requirement to drive safely.

About This Job
We're hiring a Partner Development Manager to recruit, onboard, and activate channel partners and drive partner-sourced pipeline across our target markets. This is a hands-on commercial role. You'll own the full partner lifecycle from sourcing through to revenue contribution, working closely with the CRO and the direct sales team.
Early partner relationships are already generating pipeline. This role will scale that motion across a broader portfolio of partners and build the operational rhythm to sustain it.
You will report directly to the CRO, with a defined path to Head of Channels and Alliances as the programme scales.
What you'll do
You'll recruit partners from a curated target list, prioritising cloud hyperscaler ecosystem partners, regional and multi-regional systems integrators with embedded relationships inside enterprise financial services and technology accounts, AI governance and software engineering advisory firms, and complementary SaaS vendors serving the same engineering and finance buyers with adjacent, non-competing products.
You'll run the full partner recruitment cycle from initial outreach through commercial agreement to activation. You'll enable signed partners so thoroughly that they can position BlueOptima confidently and independently. You'll build co-sell motions in lockstep with BlueOptima AEs, including cloud marketplace transactions. You'll manage marketplace listing optimisation and activation mechanics in partnership with our product and finance teams. You'll own the partner pipeline in HubSpot with full transparency and forecast accountability to the CRO every week and every quarter. You'll build and maintain the operational scaffolding of the programme: onboarding processes, enablement materials, deal registration workflows, and partner scorecards.

Qualifications
What we're looking for
Three to five years in B2B channel sales, alliances, or partner management, with demonstrable experience recruiting and onboarding new partners rather than simply managing inherited relationships. You've owned a partner-sourced pipeline number before and you're comfortable being held to one. You know the difference between a signed partner agreement and an active revenue relationship, and everything you build is oriented around the latter.
Comfort with cloud marketplace mechanics. You don't need to be an expert, but you need to understand how co-sell and marketplace transactions work. Commercial instinct and the ability to build a referral fee model, stress-test the margin assumptions, and present a commercially sound case to finance. Familiarity with enterprise software sales cycles and the confidence to run partner-facing conversations independently at a senior level. The ability to articulate a technical value proposition to non-technical partner audiences.
You build your own target list, run your own outreach, and generate pipeline independently. You do not wait for partners to come to you.
What we're not looking for
Candidates whose channel experience is primarily managing an established partner base, or working within large GSI governance structures at a mature vendor, are likely to find this role a difficult adjustment. Candidates from high-velocity SMB or transactional reseller environments will also find the transition significant. Our buyers are CTOs and CFOs at tier-one financial institutions. The sales motion is deliberate, account-based, and relationship-driven.
Nice to have
Experience in developer tooling, DevOps, engineering intelligence, or any SaaS product sold to engineering leadership. Prior experience in financial services enterprise accounts. Exposure to mid-market sales motions alongside enterprise.

Additional Information
What success looks like
You'll be measured on active partner engagement and the volume of qualified partner-sourced pipeline entering the business within your first year. A focused portfolio of active, co-selling partners and a channel motion the direct sales team trusts and wants to work alongside.

The Pressure Compliance Mechanical Engineer will report to the Pressure System Completions and Integration Manager and will take responsibility for managing the pressure systems compliance and structural integrity requirements on behalf of a specific scope identified by the Pressure System Completions and Integration Manager and Pressure Compliance Lead, ensuring appropriate implementation and compliance to meet HPC project needs.
The role holder will support the implementation of pressure systems compliance and structural integrity requirements within specific projects, on behalf of a specific programme. They will support the project managers in ensuring compliance and delivery for HPC.
The role will require good technical and organisational capabilities to effectively interface with Project Managers and relevant stakeholders in the programme, the ONR, third party organisations and support the supply chain in delivery.

This exciting role will join the payroll team and be responsible for growth and expansion into existing and new markets. You’ll attend internal and external calls, understand the payroll requirements to set up in the country and work with internal teams to support the implementation.

•
Lead end to end payroll projects supporting growth and expansion
•
Develop and manage project plans and timelines, capture risks
•
Partner with internal teams to ensure alignment in the projects

Assess payroll readiness for new markets
•
Manage external vendors

Lead build, testing and sign off for go live readiness

Monitor project risks, issues, dependencies and ensure stakeholders are updated

Support post implementation hyper care period

• We’re evolving our payroll model - you’ll have the chance to bring your brainpower and prior experience to help us build an outstanding payroll team as we continue to grow and scale

• Project Management - Experience in leading payroll projects and delivering on time

About This Job
Role overview
We’re looking for Collections Advisors to join our growing and award-winning team at Hilton Baird Collections Services, part of FRP Advisory. Working across all areas of our product portfolio, the Collections Advisor will be responsible for recovering money on behalf of our valued SME, corporate, lender and insolvency clients in the most timely, compliant and efficient manner. The role also involves meeting personal and team targets and ensuring that the highest levels of quality and professionalism are always maintained. We offer a supportive and fast-paced working environment with hybrid working opportunities. You'll also have access to professional and industry recognised qualifications.
Key Responsibilities
• Take ownership and manage a portfolio of live, current and overdue debit balance customer accounts, making 50-80 calls per day
• Obtain payments, resolve queries/disputes and where appropriate agree on payment plans in a timely and satisfactory manner
• Manage workload and prioritise tasks to meet business targets and team KPIs
• Liaise with clients and provide updates on customer accounts
• Maintain quality and professionalism while accurately controlling ledgers
• Make recommendations to improve departmental processes ensuring that debtors and bank customers are processed through the collections process as smoothly as possible
• Perform against individual targets while contributing to the overall productivity of the team
• Facilitate and record escalations and issues outside the standard processes to the Collections Manager
• Perform any duties required as part of special projects

Qualifications
• Educated to GCSE standard or above. Business or Accountancy-based qualifications are desirable
• Knowledge of credit control and experience in collections or credit control roles (legal collections experience preferred)
• Excellent communication, listening and interpersonal skills
• High attention to detail and computer proficiency (Word, Excel, Outlook, Sage or similar)
• Ability to work independently and as part of a team
• Hardworking, punctual, reliable and able to work under pressure
• Self-motivated, adaptable and eager to learn and develop

Additional Information
Our Values
• Straightforward: We provide clear, no-nonsense advice
• Confident: Our guidance is backed by expertise and evidence
• Pragmatic: We focus on practical solutions and tangible outcomes
• Real: We are professional yet approachable, understanding the challenges our clients face
Our Commitment to You and the Environment
At FRP, sustainability is integral to our strategy and operations. Our sustainability depends on building and maintaining meaningful, long-term relationships with all our stakeholders – including our employees, clients, and local communities – while also reducing our impact on the natural environment.
We are always striving to improve in all areas – whether it’s our people, our clients, our planet or our governance. Our ongoing success as a business depends on our sustainability and agility in a changing and challenging global landscape.
We are committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and diverse culture for our people. We maintain an Equal Opportunities Policy, ensuring that recruitment and employment decisions are based solely on the skills and experience required for our professional services — regardless of ethnicity, race, sexual orientation, disability, or any other protected characteristic. We believe every individual should have the opportunity to thrive.
Our learning and development programmes enable us to invest in growing our employees’ careers. We aim to empower our team members to each achieve their potential.
We are committed to growing long-term relationships with our clients and supporting them in achieving their objectives. We understand that our clients’ sustainability and success lead to our sustainability and success. We are emotionally invested in our clients right from the beginning.

What you’ll do in this role:
• Conduct functional assessments which include initial reviews, face-to-face, video or telephone assessments to evaluate how a claimant’s health condition or disability affects them for various types of benefit.
• Analyse and interpret clinical information and supporting evidence.

• Use IT systems to support clinical decision-making and report writing.

What are PIP and WCA?
• Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a benefit for people with a long-term health condition or impairment. It is paid to make a contribution to the extra costs that disabled people may face, to help them lead full, active and independent lives.
• Work Capability Assessment (WCA) is a functional assessment that looks at a range of different activities relating to physical, mental, intellectual and cognitive functions, to help DWP/DfC determine a customer's capability for work or work-related activity.

Qualifications
About you
• HCPC registered Physiotherapist with a valid PIN and no current restrictions
• Minimum of one year’s post-registration experience.
• Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
• Ability to produce clear, accurate and detailed reports.
• Comfortable working quickly to meet structured targets.
• Good IT skills including Microsoft Office, and the ability to learn new systems while working remotely.
• excellent observational and communication skills, giving you the ability to listen, empathise and dig deeper.
• A driving licence or access to transport for assessment centre working.

We deliver assessments for a variety of different benefits, including delivering PIP, WCA and Specialist benefit assessments across the Midlands and Wales, and in Northern Ireland.

•
Desirable:

Holroyd Howe is one of the UK’s leading contract caterers, providing fresh innovative food services solely to independent schools and colleges. To provide our teams with the right skills to succeed in their jobs, we invest in their training and development. Our exceptional teams of seasoned specialists customise our catering services to fit children of all ages and satisfy the unique needs of our clients.
We pride ourselves on:
Sustainability
Sustainability is at the heart of our thinking; always mindful of the ethics of our sourcing and how we prepare our meals.
Nutrition
We take nutrition seriously and understand the impact a healthy diet has on the fundamental years of development. Meals are always freshly prepared from scratch and packed with nutritious ingredients.
Food Innovation
We offer a wide portfolio of training opportunities and experiences, which attracts chefs who are passionate about culinary excellence and menu innovation to our team.
From tasting tables, theme days and food theatre, to chef demonstrations and supplier showcases, we create engaging and fun dining experiences for our students. We work together to make mealtimes exploratory, quirky, and fun for our pupils, helping them build strong and healthy relationships with food.
Holroyd Howe is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people and expect all employees to share this commitment. This search helps identify any issues that may affect suitability to work with children.

About the Role
The UK water sector is entering a period of unprecedented investment and transformation. As Egis accelerates the growth of its Water Business in the UK, we are building a high-performing Process Engineering team to help shape this next chapter.
We are inviting applicants who want to play a meaningful role in delivering major water and wastewater programmes in the UK municipal and industrial sectors. • Lead process design delivery on multidisciplinary water/wastewater treatment projects across the full design lifecycle.

• Review and approve process calculations, mass balances, PFDs, P&IDs, basis of design reports, specifications, technical notes, models and supplier/contractor submissions.
• Lead process modelling and simulation activities using tools such as BioWin, SUMO, Dynamizu or equivalent packages.
• Lead optioneering, process capacity assessments, value engineering, design reviews, HAZOP/SWIFT, commissioning strategy and performance testing input.
• Drive multidisciplinary coordination across Mechanical, EICA, civil/structural, architectural, MEP, construction, commissioning and operations teams.
• Promote lean and digitally enabled delivery through standardised tools, process models, automation, data analysis and reusable templates.

• Mentor and manage engineers where appropriate, supporting recruitment, development and chartership progression.
• Contribute to bids, client engagement, opportunity shaping and growth of the process capability.

Qualifications
Minimum Requirements
• BEng/MEng or equivalent in Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering or closely related discipline.
• Chartered Engineer or Incorporated Engineer status with a relevant professional institution, such as IChemE.
• Typically 8–10+ years’ relevant process design experience.
• Background must be from water, wastewater and/or biosolids/sludge treatment design.
• Proven ability to act as process discipline lead or senior technical lead on multidisciplinary projects.
• Strong technical expertise in water/wastewater treatment process design, including process selection, mass balance, process capacity, PFDs, P&IDs and design basis development.
• Practical experience using process modelling/simulation packages such as BioWin, SUMO, Dynamizu or equivalent.
• Strong understanding of UK water industry standards, CDM 2015, process safety, safety-by-design, regulatory drivers and common delivery models.
• Confident client-facing communicator with experience leading workshops, technical reviews and design discussions.
• Experience mentoring or managing engineers and supporting technical capability development.
Desirable Skills / Knowledge
• Deep experience in wastewater treatment, clean water treatment, sludge/bioresources, nutrient removal, water reuse/recycling, process optimisation, chemical dosing, energy recovery or low-carbon design.
• Experience delivering AMP8, WINEP, SRO, D&B, framework, alliance or contractor-led projects.
• Advanced capability in BioWin, SUMO, Dynamizu, process model calibration, scenario testing, dynamic simulation or operational optimisation.
• Experience developing process design standards, calculation tools, modelling workflows, QA processes or reusable digital templates.
• Experience contributing to recruitment, resource planning, bid writing, technical proposals, client presentations or new service development.

In each project we design, engineer and operate we care deeply about the legacy we’re leaving behind. As part of our team, you’ll have a unique opportunity to use your skills and expertise to shape a better future for our communities in the UK, and all around the globe.

About This Job
About the Role
As Senior Legal Counsel, you’ll sit within the ASOS Legal Team. This is a permanent, senior legal role covering a broad range of general commercial matters.
You will be a key point of contact across a number of business areas which may include, for example, Commercial/Retail, Supply Chain, Marketing, Payments, Technology, and Consumer Regulation. Previous experience across every area of practice is not a requirement, but the successful candidate will need to be comfortable with taking the initiative across a diverse range of matters.
This is a high-impact, commercially focused role requiring 6+ years’ PQE. You will report to a Head of Legal. You will also supervise junior members of the team, so people management skills are a prerequisite.
The role is critical in helping the wider ASOS Legal Team meet the needs and requirements of all elements of ASOS’ business across the globe, requiring the ability to give commercial as well as legal advice, often on cross-border matters, and to promptly identify risks and issues that need to be escalated within the company.
The role requires someone who is hands-on and commercially minded, with a strong professional ethic and the energy, interest, and training to pursue a huge array of legal and commercial challenges. You’ll need to be technically excellent and able to give commercial as well as legal advice, operate comfortably on cross-border matters, and promptly identify risks and issues for escalation to appropriate senior stakeholders.
Flexibility and adaptability are essential – the successful candidate must be comfortable picking up work across any area of the business. ASOS is fast paced, so all employees need to be adaptable and enthused about what’s around the corner for us. We work in a highly collaborative environment, presenting numerous opportunities to enjoy a wide variety of often innovative legal and commercial challenges.
The details
This is a general commercial role, and we have set out some examples of the types of work that this role may involve.
Commercial & Supply Chain
• Supporting ASOS on its wholesale, third party brands, flex fulfilment models and sourcing teams across the full range of commercial matters.
• Advising on the commercial supplier lifecycle process, including onboarding, T&Cs negotiations, policies, supplier compliance, exit strategies, and any disputes.
• Advising on, drafting, and negotiating global supply chain contracts for the supply of a wide range of goods and services required to get products from the manufacturer to the customer’s doorstep.
• Negotiating long-term agreements with global logistics services providers to operate warehouses, and contracts for the supply and installation of warehouse equipment.
• Advising on global compliance issues and product safety matters, including managing and supervising escalated customer complaints.
Marketing & Consumer
• Working collectively with the Procurement Team to provide legal support on a broad range of commercial contracts including adtech, affiliate relationships, brand partnerships, public relations, and creative agencies, while ensuring all critical commercial and regulatory requirements are appropriately covered.
• Negotiating contracts and IP rights relating to marketing and customer-facing projects.
• Working closely with marketing and media teams to ensure ASOS’s global marketing campaigns and commercial partnerships are compliant with relevant advertising regulations across multiple territories, including copy clearance and managing any ASA or CMA complaints.
• Advising the business on consumer regulation compliance, including consumer rights, digital markets/services regulations, green claims regimes, online practices regulations (e.g., dark patterns), pricing regulations, and other relevant frameworks. Managing regulatory and consumer complaints/litigation.
• Global horizon scanning of upcoming regulation and project managing the implementation of new regulations across internal business stakeholders.
Technology & Payments
• Reviewing, drafting, and negotiating the full range of technology contracts, including software development and licensing, SaaS, PaaS, HaaS, service level agreements, telecoms, consultancy services, outsourcing, and hardware provision.
• Advising on the implementation of technology programs across business functions (e.g., Retail Management Systems, Warehouse Management Systems, Finance Systems, and People Team platforms).
• Working closely with Technology teams to assist with the development of ASOS’s ecommerce offerings (website, mobile web, apps) and advising on new technologies, including opportunities and inherent risks.
• Supporting the due diligence and commercial analysis for start-up partnerships and/or acquisitions, and proof of concept phases for new technology.
• Advising on payments-related matters across the business.
Team & Management
• Reporting to a Head of Legal, with the opportunity to work closely with the General Counsel and Company Secretary.
• Managing junior team members, so people management skills are a prerequisite.
• Building and maintaining strong relationships with internal stakeholders and external counsel across all levels and geographies.
• Managing legal and commercial aspects of critical projects and acting as the key point of contact to drive projects forward with multiple stakeholders.
• Identifying the need for external legal advice and escalating legal matters accordingly.
• Identifying and helping to prepare and deliver training to the Legal Team and to the wider business on relevant legal and commercial issues.

Qualifications
About you
• Broad general commercial legal experience gained from private practice and/or in-house positions. Previous experience across every area of practice is not a requirement – but the role will suit someone who loves job variety and working across multiple business areas.
• 6+ years’ PQE, qualified solicitor in England & Wales (or equivalent qualification outside of England & Wales).
• Previous experience working in a fast-paced, growing, agile in-house commercial environment is preferred.
• Exposure to retail, ecommerce, or consumer-facing businesses is highly desirable.
• Excellent IT skills, particularly in relation to SharePoint, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint. An enthusiastic early adopter of new technology, including AI tools and emerging legal technology – comfort and curiosity with AI-assisted workflows is a real plus.
• An excellent communicator who is approachable and adaptable, building relationships at all levels across the business and across geographies. Able to adapt communication style to interact effectively with a wide variety of people and personalities within the unique environment of ASOS.
• Energy and drive to succeed – comfortable with change and enthused about what’s around the corner for us.
• Experience in the maintenance and development of agreement templates and contract playbooks.

The post holder ensures robust cost governance, accurate measurement and valuation, effective change control, and proactive commercial risk management, in line with RICS professional standards, organisational governance, and regulatory requirements (including PA23 where applicable).

Cost Management & Commercial Control
With respect to low value and low complexity contracts and package orders:

• Cost plans and cost breakdown structures

Measurement, Valuation & Change Control
With respect to low value and low complexity contracts and package orders:

Contract & Procurement Support

Risk, Claims & Dispute Management

Reporting, Governance & Assurance

Stakeholder Management & Leadership

About This Job
About us
Fusion, the process that powers the sun and stars, is one of the most promising options for generating the cleaner, carbon-free energy that our world badly needs. UKAEA leads the way in realizing fusion energy, partnering with industry and research organisations to achieve ground-breaking advancements. Our goal is to bring fusion electricity to the grid by developing the power stations of tomorrow and the skilled workforce to deliver them.
About the job
We are seeking a Senior Testing Rigs & Labs Technician to provide advanced hands‑on technical support within our experimental laboratories and workshop.
In this role, you will play a key part in building, operating and maintaining testing rigs and laboratory systems that support prototype development and experimental programmes. You will work closely with engineers, scientists and other technicians, applying practical expertise to ensure experiments are delivered safely, efficiently and to a high technical standard.
You will act as a subject‑matter specialist in defined areas of laboratory practice, take ownership of discrete work activities, and support the development of junior technicians and apprentices.
What You’ll Be Doing
• Carry out hands‑on laboratory and experimental work, including fabrication, assembly, integration, commissioning, operation and decommissioning of testing rigs and equipment
• Support the safe and effective day‑to‑day operation of testing rigs and laboratory facilities
• Apply practical mechanical and/or electrical expertise to translate drawings, schematics and test plans into robust physical setups
• Identify and resolve technical issues during builds and experimental operations, escalating novel or higher‑risk problems as required
• Contribute to risk assessments, method statements and safe systems of work within laboratory environments
• Take responsibility for defined operational areas such as tooling, consumables, equipment organisation or calibration coordination
• Maintain accurate records for equipment status, servicing, calibration and experimental activities
• Support the collection, handling and basic processing of experimental data
• Contribute practical input to experimental planning, design reviews and operational improvement activities
• Guide and mentor junior technicians and apprentices, promoting good laboratory practice and safe working
• Work collaboratively with engineers and stakeholders, communicating clearly and professionally
What You’ll Bring
• Relevant technical qualification in a STEM discipline (e.g. HNC/HND or equivalent experience)
• Proven hands‑on experience in laboratory, workshop, prototype or experimental test environments
• Strong mechanical and/or electrical skills (ideally both), with the ability to work confidently from technical drawings and documentation
• Experience assembling, commissioning, operating or maintaining test rigs or experimental equipment
• Awareness of laboratory hazards (e.g. pressure systems, vacuum, cryogenic, high‑voltage systems) and safe working practices
• Experience contributing to risk assessments and safety documentation
• Ability to work independently within established procedures and manage competing tasks
• Clear written and verbal communication skills
• Experience supporting or guiding less‑experienced colleagues
UKAEA is an onsite organisation, and this role requires regular onsite presence (usually between 3-5 days in any given week) in line with business needs. We actively support flexible working arrangements where this is compatible with the role.
Benefits
We have a generous range of benefits (see the full list here) and highlights include:
• A salary of £43, 702 (inclusive of a 3,300 specialist allowance)
• Up to 7% corporate performance bonus
• Final salary defined benefits pension scheme with an equivalent of 21.5% employer pension contribution
• 25 days annual leave plus 2.5 'privilege' days; 8 Bank Holidays
• Additional 3 days of site closure over Christmas break
• Flexible working options plus family-friendly leave provisions
Our commitment to ED&I
UKAEA's mission is clean energy for all, and we welcome talented people from all backgrounds to help us achieve this goal. We are committed to equality, diversity, inclusion and accessibility, and strive to ensure fair representation across our workforce.
Please email talent@ukaea.uk if you have any questions or require adjustments to help you participate fairly in our recruitment process, for example changes to the way we interview or share information. As a Disability Confident Employer, we are committed to providing an inclusive and accessible recruitment experience for all candidates.
We particularly encourage applications from groups currently underrepresented in STEM, including women and people from diverse ethnic backgrounds. All appointments are made on merit and further information can be found here.

So, what's the job really about?
Well, imagine popping by to help Mrs. Smith start her day. One moment you're assisting her out of bed and helping her choose an outfit, and the next, you're sharing a cuppa and a natter as she enjoys her breakfast. Later, you might be off to Mr. Jones' to make sure he's got his medication sorted and a hot meal on the table. Maybe a quick tidy-up, or a trip to the shops is on the cards as well.

Our visits are never less than an hour, allowing plenty of time to provide quality care without feeling rushed. You ensure all of your clients are comfortable and safe to enable them to stay independent in their own homes.

• Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.

You will sit at the intersection of social management, editorial storytelling, and performance insight, ensuring everything we publish is grounded in a clear brand point of view, optimised for how audiences behave across platforms, and delivering against both brand and content KPIs. Working closely with the Editorial Manager and Community Manager, you will help ensure ASOS’s editorial voice is expressed consistently, confidently, and with genuine fashion authority everywhere our audience encounters us.
Why This Role Matters
Social and Editorial content is at the core of ASOS’s transformation into a leading style authority and cultural fashion destination. This role is critical in ensuring that our content output is:
• Consistently high quality, on brand, and editorially led
• Aligned to platform behaviours and trends
• Platform-native and responsive to cultural moments in real time
• Informed by performance insights and audience intelligence
• Driving measurable impact across engagement, reach, and brand consideration
By connecting social-first execution with editorial thinking and insight-led optimisation, you will help ensure ASOS shows up with a distinct point of view, at the right time, with content that resonates and builds brand equity and fame over time.
What You Will Be Responsible For
Content & Strategy
• Interpret briefs and build detailed content plans that bring ASOS storytelling to life across social channels.
• Contribute original ideas to social and editorial content planning, with a strong understanding of social-first storytelling, fashion trends, and what resonates with a 20-something audience.
• Ensure all content output is platform-native, on-brand, and aligned to the ASOS brand strategy and tone of voice guidelines.
• Support the delivery of social activity across key brand campaigns and franchises by clearly briefing creative teams, external agencies and talent.
• Support the development of franchises and recurring content formats that build audience recognition and compound brand equity over time.
Channel Management and Content Production
• Support the delivery of content across key brand campaigns, always-on moments, and franchises.
• Own day-to-day curation, publishing, scheduling and tagging across all channels.
• Write and edit captions, scripts, and copy for social content, ensuring tone of voice is consistently applied with personality, authority, and genuine fashion credibility.
• Work closely with the Community Manager to ensure published content and community engagement tell a coherent, consistent brand story across all channels.
• Support with the maintenance of the content calendar in collaboration with the wider Social and Editorial team.
Performance & Optimisation
• Monitor content performance across key metrics (engagement, reach, saves, shares, view rate), and feed learnings back into content planning to continuously improve output quality.
• Work with the Social Optimisation Manager to translate data into actionable improvements, refining formats, captions, hooks, and posting approaches.
• Support with the maintenance of the content calendar in collaboration with the wider Social and Editorial team.
• Stay ahead of platform updates, emerging social behaviours, and fashion and cultural moments, proactively bringing insights and opportunities into the team.

Collaboration & Cross-Functional Working

As a graduate within SESA, you will work across the engineering lifecycle alongside disciplines such as signalling, telecommunications, rolling stock, track, civils, stations, power, operations and maintenance.

jobs.smartrecruiters.com/turnertownsend/.description_excerpt:
About This Job
Due to increased opportunities and demand in the Energy & Natural Resources division, the Energy & Natural Resources team are recruiting a Project Planner to join a diverse and supportive team during a period of significant growth. Our nuclear client is at the forefront of industry leading change, and we are keen to speak to individuals with project planning experience to see what Turner & Townsend can offer you. Candidates will be required to be present in our client office for 3 days per week.
MAIN PURPOSE OF ROLE
A Planner will be responsible for work packages and projects of varying size and complexity. Due to the nature of the programme of works, work packages may vary in size with Planners accountable for scheduling multiple smaller projects or one which could be significantly larger in value. A Planner will be responsible for taking the lead on planning for multiple non-related projects or single highly complex projects within the programme of works. They will understand and manage relationships between time, cost, risk, change, reporting and scope, with accountability for creating and maintaining robust schedules that provide our clients with accurate data to drive management decisions. They will play a key role in ensuring that client objectives are met and that projects are delivered to time and cost targets and the appropriate quality standards.
KEY ACCOUNTABILITIES
• As a Planner, you have a passion to provide services as required by our clients, which may include:
• Taking the lead on planning, supporting more junior planning professionals on novel, high value projects or programmes.
• Creation, development and maintenance of project schedules that assist and align with project requirements on a complex, risk managed project or programme.
• Adherence to NEC or FIDIC contract processes for management of schedule data and submissions.
• Assisting the project team to develop status reports to keep management informed on project progress.
• Involvement with senior team in oversight of day-to-day management, staffing and the implementation of Integrated Project Controls standards and processes.
• Reducing uncertainty, improving efficiency and understanding project objectives.
• Interacting with the project team to define scope of work to develop and update detailed schedules, cost information and identification of variances from original schedule.
• Assisting project managers to schedule work and coordinate assignments.
• Evaluation of project schedule progress and performance and identify developing problem areas.
• Analysis of float, critical path and constraints to understand the effect of approved changes or slippages to schedule, recommending alternative courses of action for recovery.
• Undertaking project progress reviews.
• Monitoring and consolidation of multiple project schedules into Integrated master Schedule (IMS).
• Monitoring the project managers reporting system summarising the progress status of all projects.
• Monitor and advise on status of project KPIs across multiple projects.
• Understand and report EVM on a periodic basis.
• Functional management of planning personnel within the Turner & Townsend team, conducting mentoring and coaching as required.

Qualifications
You have professional Project Controls experience specialising in Planning & Scheduling in one or more sectors across the whole Project lifecycle. While nuclear experience is desirable it is not an absolute requirement. You have strong knowledge and proficiency with Primavera (P6) and other planning and resourcing software and can coordinate and work with other teams utilising your multi-disciplinary knowledge.
You will be a strong communicator, able to demonstrate leadership behaviours with the ability to influence, manage, motivate, coach and develop a team by fostering a diverse and inclusive environment. You promote empowerment and contribution and have a passion to build a community and support network beyond your delivery role.
You also;
• Will be able to obtain BPSS level security clearance.
• Are a member of a relevant professional body e.g., Association for Project Management, Project Management Institute.
• Have excellent verbal and written communication skills.
• Have the ability to make risk-based decisions where the parameters are unclear, and judgement is needed.
• Have strong leadership skills with the ability to mobilise, inspire and lead by example.
• Have strong stakeholder management experience.
• Can navigate through conflict situations and defuse tension.
• Have a desire to work within the nuclear sector.

Additional Information
Our inspired people share our vision and mission. We provide a great place to work, where each person has the opportunity and voice to affect change.
We want our people to succeed both in work and life. To support this we promote a healthy, productive and flexible working environment that respects work-life balance.
Turner & Townsend is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and actively encourage applications from all sectors of the community.
Please find out more about us at www.turnerandtownsend.com/
Join our social media conversations for more information about Turner & Townsend and our exciting future projects:
Twitter
Instagram
LinkedIn
